name: Grins
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village with a medieval old town center, a historic castle, and one of the most beautiful village squares in Tirol.
beschreibung:
Overview

Grins is situated on a sun-drenched plateau at 1,006 metres elevation in the Tyrolean district of Landeck, roughly five kilometres west of the district capital Landeck. Home to approximately 1,400 residents, this peaceful mountain village sprawls across the sunny balcony at the entrance to the Stanzer Valley at the foot of the rugged Lechtal Alps, crowned by the 2,473-metre Lattenkopf. Due to its protected mountainside exposure, Grins enjoys an exceptionally mild microclimate that has supported traditional fruit and plum orchards for centuries. Celebrated as Tyrol's only officially certified healing water village, Grins brings together therapeutic mineral springs, romantic gorges, and ancient traditions. The village architecture is defined by stately whitewashed farmsteads in the Rhaeto-Romanic Upper Inn Valley style, adorned with ornate sgraffiti, bay windows, and arched portals.

History

Settlement on this mountain terrace dates back to pre-Roman times; the name Grins derives from the Celtic-Rhaetian term crines, meaning a rock cleft or fissure, referring to the rugged Albinschlucht gorge. The community was first recorded in 1288 as Grinnes in the comprehensive land register of Count Meinhard II of Tyrol. From 1330 onward, the primary transalpine packhorse trade route across the Arlberg Pass passed directly through the village; from the mid-16th century dates the iconic stone arched bridge spanning the Mühlbach gorge, known locally as the Roman Bridge (Römerbrücke), which now forms the municipal coat of arms. A historic treasure is the mineral spring first documented in 1372, where according to legend Countess Margarete Maultasch bathed, giving rise to the historic Wildbad Grins thermal bath. Following a devastating fire in 1945, the village center was lovingly reconstructed in traditional style. The parish church of St. Nicholas features a Gothic spire, an exquisite 1779 Rococo nave by Franz Singer, and ceiling frescoes by master Matthäus Günther. The centuries-old spring ritual of disc-flinging (Scheibenschlagen) is recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Grins via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and the Arlberg Expressway S16, taking the Landeck-West or Pians/Grins exit. From there, the provincial road L256 winds uphill for just five to eight minutes to the plateau. Rail passengers travel to the major international railway hub of Landeck-Zams, which offers direct Railjet and Eurocity train connections across Austria and Europe. From the station square, regional VVT bus route 4242 runs frequent services taking just 12 minutes to reach the village square and the thermal bath area in Grins, free of charge for holders of the regional TirolWest Card.

Tips

A rejuvenating experience awaits in the romantic Albinschlucht gorge, where visitors explore the mystical Albigen Legend Trail dedicated to nature spirits, admire the rocky Schellenloch fissure, and enjoy the therapeutic waters in the modern Kneipp outdoor water facility. A short stroll leads to the historic Roman Bridge overlooking the roaring stream. Experienced hikers climb in about two and a half hours to the Grinner Hütte alpine lodge at 1,793 metres, a panoramic base for tackling the 2,473-metre Lattenkopf summit with breathtaking vistas over the Stanzer Valley and the Verwall Alps. Grins also lies directly along renowned long-distance trails, including the Tyrolean Way of St. James and the Starkenberg Panorama Trail.
